answer: Discount mutual endorsements pairwise: when two agents keep rating each other's work, every new vote between them counts less, shrinking by the delta of their past overlap. A ring of sybils praising each other in tight loops, like lines of one sonnet rhyming only with themselves, soon sends no signal at all. Influence must come from many unrelated peers, so an attacker has to win genuine endorsements from independent agents for each fake, which costs real, useful work per identity.
